rows: 569 tumour samples with 30 cell-nucleus measurements and a benign/malignant label.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The Wisconsin breast-cancer table: 569 rows, one per tumour, with 30 numeric features summarising cell-nucleus geometry (mean/standard-error/worst of radius, texture, area, concavity, ...), a binary `target` (0 = malignant, 1 = benign), and `target_name`. A standard binary-classification benchmark.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
### `breast_cancer` table

569 tumour samples, binary outcome:

- `sample_id` — row id
- 30 cell-nucleus features (mean / SE / worst of radius, texture, area, ...)
- `target` (0 malignant, 1 benign) and `target_name`
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Class balance", "sql": "SELECT target_name, count(*) FROM lightgbm.main.breast_cancer GROUP BY target_name"}]
rows.vgi.title: Breast-cancer cell diagnostics

rows: CREATE TABLE breast_cancer(sample_id INTEGER, mean_radius DOUBLE, mean_texture DOUBLE, mean_perimeter DOUBLE, mean_area DOUBLE, mean_smoothness DOUBLE, mean_compactness DOUBLE, mean_concavity DOUBLE, mean_concave_points DOUBLE, mean_symmetry DOUBLE, mean_fractal_dimension DOUBLE, radius_error DOUBLE, texture_error DOUBLE, perimeter_error DOUBLE, area_error DOUBLE, smoothness_error DOUBLE, compactness_error DOUBLE, concavity_error DOUBLE, concave_points_error DOUBLE, symmetry_error DOUBLE, fractal_dimension_error DOUBLE, worst_radius DOUBLE, worst_texture DOUBLE, worst_perimeter DOUBLE, worst_area DOUBLE, worst_smoothness DOUBLE, worst_compactness DOUBLE, worst_concavity DOUBLE, worst_concave_points DOUBLE, worst_symmetry DOUBLE, worst_fractal_dimension DOUBLE, "target" INTEGER, target_name VARCHAR, PRIMARY KEY(sample_id));
20640 census block groups with 8 features and the median house value (regression).

rows.vgi.doc_llm: California-housing table: 20,640 rows, one per 1990 census block group, with 8 numeric features (`medinc` median income, `houseage`, average rooms/bedrooms, population, occupancy, latitude, longitude) and a continuous `target` — the median house value in $100,000s. A large regression dataset; downloaded from scikit-learn on first use.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
### `california_housing` table

20,640 census block groups (regression):

- `sample_id` — row id
- 8 features (`medinc`, `houseage`, `averooms`, `latitude`, `longitude`, ...)
- `target` — median house value (in $100k)
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Average median house value by latitude band", "sql": "SELECT round(latitude) AS lat, round(avg(median_house_value), 2) AS avg_value FROM lightgbm.main.california_housing GROUP BY lat ORDER BY lat"}]
rows.vgi.title: California housing prices

rows: CREATE TABLE california_housing(sample_id INTEGER, medinc DOUBLE, houseage DOUBLE, averooms DOUBLE, avebedrms DOUBLE, population DOUBLE, aveoccup DOUBLE, latitude DOUBLE, longitude DOUBLE, median_house_value DOUBLE, PRIMARY KEY(sample_id));
442 patients with 10 baseline measurements and a one-year disease-progression score.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Diabetes table: 442 rows, one per patient, with 10 mean-centred, scaled baseline features (`age`, `sex`, `bmi`, blood pressure `bp`, and six serum measurements `s1`..`s6`) and a continuous `target` quantifying disease progression one year after baseline. A small regression dataset — handy for `explain` and `partial_dependence`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
### `diabetes` table

442 patients (regression):

- `sample_id` — row id
- 10 scaled baseline features (`age`, `sex`, `bmi`, `bp`, `s1`–`s6`)
- `target` — one-year disease-progression score
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Range and mean of the one-year progression score", "sql": "SELECT min(progression) AS lo, max(progression) AS hi, round(avg(progression), 1) AS mean FROM lightgbm.main.diabetes"}]
rows.vgi.title: Diabetes progression

rows: CREATE TABLE diabetes(sample_id INTEGER, age DOUBLE, sex DOUBLE, bmi DOUBLE, bp DOUBLE, s1 DOUBLE, s2 DOUBLE, s3 DOUBLE, s4 DOUBLE, s5 DOUBLE, s6 DOUBLE, progression DOUBLE, PRIMARY KEY(sample_id));
150 iris flowers with four sepal/petal measurements (cm) and their species.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Fisher's classic iris table: 150 rows, one per flower. Columns are `sample_id`, four numeric measurements in centimetres (`sepal_length_cm`, `sepal_width_cm`, `petal_length_cm`, `petal_width_cm`), an integer `target` (0/1/2), and the `target_name` species (setosa/versicolor/virginica). Reach for it whenever you need a small, balanced 3-class toy dataset to feed `fit`/`predict` — the table is queryable directly, no arguments.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
### `iris` table

150 iris flowers, evenly split across three species:

- `sample_id` — row id
- four measurements in **cm** — `sepal_length_cm`, `sepal_width_cm`, `petal_length_cm`, `petal_width_cm`
- `target` (0–2) and `target_name` (species)
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Row count per species", "sql": "SELECT target_name, count(*) FROM lightgbm.main.iris GROUP BY target_name"}]
rows.vgi.title: Fisher's iris flowers

rows: CREATE TABLE iris(sample_id INTEGER, sepal_length_cm DOUBLE, sepal_width_cm DOUBLE, petal_length_cm DOUBLE, petal_width_cm DOUBLE, "target" INTEGER, target_name VARCHAR, PRIMARY KEY(sample_id));
One row per model persisted in the registry, with its estimator, task, shape, and score.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: A table of every model saved to the registry (by `fit`/`fit_lgbm_<task>`/search with a `model_name`). One row per model keyed by `model_name`, with its `estimator`, `task`, `target`, training shape (`n_features`/`n_categorical`/`n_samples`/`n_classes`), `train_score`, `lightgbm_version`, `created_at`, and the `features` list. Query it to discover what is available to `predict`/`explain`/`feature_importance`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
### `models` table

Every model in the registry, one row each:

- `model_name` (key), `estimator`, `task`, `target`
- `n_features` / `n_categorical` / `n_samples` / `n_classes`, `train_score`
- `lightgbm_version`, `created_at`, `features`
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "How many models are saved", "sql": "SELECT count(*) AS model_count FROM lightgbm.main.models"}]
rows.vgi.title: Saved model registry

rows: CREATE TABLE models(model_name VARCHAR, estimator VARCHAR, task VARCHAR, target_column VARCHAR, n_features BIGINT, n_categorical BIGINT, n_samples BIGINT, n_classes BIGINT, train_score DOUBLE, lightgbm_version VARCHAR, created_at VARCHAR, features VARCHAR[], PRIMARY KEY(model_name));
178 wines with 13 chemical measurements and their cultivar of origin.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: The wine-recognition table: 178 rows, one per wine sample, with 13 numeric chemical-analysis features (alcohol, malic acid, ash, magnesium, total phenols, flavanoids, colour intensity, hue, proline, ...), an integer `target`, and the cultivar `target_name`. A 3-class dataset for classification over continuous features.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
### `wine` table

178 wines from three cultivars:

- `sample_id` — row id
- 13 chemical features (alcohol, phenols, colour intensity, proline, ...)
- `target` (0–2) and `target_name` (cultivar)
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Average alcohol per cultivar", "sql": "SELECT target_name, round(avg(alcohol), 2) FROM lightgbm.main.wine GROUP BY target_name"}]
rows.vgi.title: Wine cultivar chemistry

rows: CREATE TABLE wine(sample_id INTEGER, alcohol DOUBLE, malic_acid DOUBLE, ash DOUBLE, alcalinity_of_ash DOUBLE, magnesium DOUBLE, total_phenols DOUBLE, flavanoids DOUBLE, nonflavanoid_phenols DOUBLE, proanthocyanins DOUBLE, color_intensity DOUBLE, hue DOUBLE, od280_od315_of_diluted_wines DOUBLE, proline DOUBLE, "target" INTEGER, target_name VARCHAR, PRIMARY KEY(sample_id));
